original_question: In tensor-product numerical integration problems on reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, Theorem 2 gives lower bounds of the form e(n,F_d)^2 >= 1 - n prod_{i=1}^d (1+alpha_i^2)^(-1) under explicit Hilbert-space assumptions on the representers and orthonormal functions. Do analogous worst-case lower bounds exist for comparable integration problems on Banach spaces, rather than Hilbert spaces?
target_in_paper: Open Problem immediately after Theorem 2 in Section 2 (the same result appears as Theorem 2.2 in the arXiv HTML rendering): whether lower bounds analogous to the Hilbert/RKHS tensor-product bounds just proved also exist for Banach spaces. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant theorem/open-problem pair in Section 2, correctly isolates the product-form bound e(n,F_d)^2 >= 1 - n prod_i (1 + alpha_i^2)^(-1), and correctly recognizes that the paper's question is about extending this Hilbert-space lower-bound phenomenon to Banach spaces. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))
missing_details: The theorem is set in spaces of real-valued functions H_i on domains D_i with continuous point evaluations, so each H_i is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))

The operator is not described only as 'numerical integration': for each i there is a bounded linear functional tilde S_i on H_i of unit norm with nonnegative representer h_i, and the d-variate problem is the tensor-product functional S_d = tilde S_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ tilde S_d on the unit ball of F_d = H_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ H_d. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))

The structural hypotheses are specific: there must exist f_i, g_i in H_i and alpha_i in (0,1] such that (h_i, f_i, g_i) is orthonormal in H_i and alpha_i h_i = f_i^2 + g_i^2. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))

The lower bound concerns the deterministic worst-case minimal error e(n,F_d) for algorithms based on n function values, with e(n,F_d) defined in Section 1. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))

Your phrase 'comparable integration problems' is vaguer than the paper: the official open problem is tethered to the specific tensor-product quadrature/integration lower bounds established just before it. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))

The paper's official formulation is narrower than a general Banach-space program: it asks only whether 'similar lower bounds' exist for Banach spaces, not for unrelated notions of tractability or for arbitrary non-Hilbert operator problems. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))
refined_question: Let H_i be reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of real-valued functions on D_i, and for each i let tilde S_i be a bounded linear functional of unit norm with nonnegative representer h_i. Assume there exist f_i, g_i in H_i and alpha_i in (0,1] such that (h_i, f_i, g_i) is orthonormal in H_i and alpha_i h_i = f_i^2 + g_i^2. For the tensor-product problem S_d = tilde S_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ tilde S_d on the unit ball of F_d = H_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ H_d, Theorem 2 proves the worst-case lower bound e(n,F_d)^2 >= 1 - n prod_{i=1}^d (1 + alpha_i^2)^(-1). Does an analogous Banach-space lower-bound theory exist for this same kind of tensor-product quadrature/integration problem; that is, can one obtain similar worst-case lower bounds for Banach spaces in place of Hilbert spaces? ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))
justification: The draft is targeting the open problem stated immediately after the theorem it paraphrases. Section 1 defines e(n,F_d) as the minimal deterministic worst-case error of n function-value algorithms. In Section 2, the paper specializes to RKHS-based quadrature formulas, explains the kernel-matrix positivity viewpoint behind the Hilbert-space lower bounds, states Theorem 2 with the precise tensor-product assumptions above, and then asks whether similar lower bounds exist for Banach spaces. So the sharp, paper-faithful rewrite should keep the Banach-space question explicitly tied to that theorem's tensor-product lower-bound setup and should not broaden it beyond the paper's one-sentence open problem. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))
